messages.subject: all measurement invarince forms in mirt
parts:
Dear Phil

I want to check all of the bellow measurement invariance forms by 'mirt'. i can not find any example for some of them in mirt manual. can 'mirt' handle all of them? any help?

1- Conﬁgural Invariance
2- Weak Invariance
3- Strong Invariance
4- Strict Invariance
5- Invariance of the Factor Variance-Covariance Matrixes
6- Latent Mean Invariance

messages.subject: Re: all measurement invarince forms in mirt
parts:
Dear Phil
I think you have some examples in mirt manual for the first four cases. hear is some briefly definition from appendix c of attached article:

1- Conﬁgural Invariance=no constrain or as you called it separate analysis for each group

2- Weak Invariance= metric invaraince= Constrain item slopes equal across groups 
 
3- Strong Invariance= scalar invaraince=Constrain item intercepts and slopes equal across groups

4- Strict Invariance=in addition to items' slopes and intercepts constrain item residual variances to be equal across groups,  

5- Invariance of the Factor Variance-Covariance Matrixes=in addition to items' slopes, intercepts and residual constrain  factor variances and covariances to be equal across groups. it is also informative to test whether the full variance/covariance matrix is also invariant across groups. This is done by adding equality constraints on the factor covariances and by fixing all factor variances to one in all groups.
 


6- Latent Mean Invariance=factor means were constrained to equality across groups (i.e., fixed to zero in all groups).

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: all measurement invarince forms in mirt
parts:
These definitions are strongly linked to SEM models, or at least only really apply to slope-intercept only items like the 2PLM/graded response/GPCMs in the IRT context (e.g., if you use a 3PLM across multiple groups, what would the definition be to constrain all the slopes and guessing parameters but free the intercepts?). Also, #4 isn't possible to define in IRT since there is no freely estimable residual variance as this is determined entirely by the expected values, and I think #3 should also freely estimate the latent mean/variance in the focal groups in order to work properly. 5) and 6) are achieved by omitting the 'free_means' and 'free_var' invariance inputs in the multipleGroup() function after declaring that all items are "anchors" and therefore invariant. HTH.

Phil
